banker_read.verdict: On the Q1 2026 print NPLs sit at 32.26%, CAR (Capital Adequacy Ratio) 1.56% on the Q3 2025 read — 844bp below the 10% floor, a cushion gone rather than thin. Neither refreshes until Q2 disclosure; Midas Financing's auditor liquidity flag is the non-bank edge of the same freeze.

tldr: The book holds frozen — NPL 32.26% on Q1, CAR 844bp under the floor.
analysis: The banking book is frozen and the freeze is the story: NPLs 32.26% on the Q1 2026 read, system CAR 1.56% on Q3 2025 — 844bp below the 10% floor, a cushion gone rather than thin. Neither moves until Q2 disclosure lands the court-stayed loan stock that already understates the printed ratio. What moves is the forward vector, and it is broadening: RMG exports to the EU fell 16.4% in H1, thinning receivables, while Midas Financing's auditor flags a liquidity gap and warns on client confidence — non-bank finance distress at name level as the resolution regime is tested. Private credit at a 33-year-low 4.98% says weak sheets cannot out-grow their bad-loan stock. Dispersion stays the trade: own the private compounders, fade the SCB paper resolution tests first.

verdict: Taka firms to 122.78 as dollar demand ebbs — demand-led calm.

risk: Demand-led taka strength masking a reserve buffer no longer topped up

banker_read.verdict: The taka firmed to 122.78 from 123.20, but the driver is soft import demand, not abundant earned dollars — a cooling economy pulling less. Reserves $36.42bn on the 31 Jul print, cover 6.28mo, the August refresh overdue against a $1.77bn trade gap. Calm, but demand-led.

tldr: Taka firms to 122.78 on soft dollar demand; gold rebounds to $4,437.
analysis: The taka's strength is real but its source matters. USD/BDT firmed to 122.78 from 123.20 — not on a surge of earned dollars but because importer demand ebbed, a cooling economy drawing fewer letters of credit as private credit sits at a 33-year-low 4.98%. That is demand-led calm, and it flatters a buffer not being topped up. The inflow side thins in parallel: July remittance held $2.82bn, a second month under $3bn, and RMG exports to the EU fell 16.4% in H1. Reserves stood at $36.42bn on the 31 Jul print, cover 6.28mo, and the August refresh is overdue — a figure below $36bn would confirm the drain the soft trade data imply. The desk position: respect 122.78 as a level, but treat the reserve refresh, not the daily spot, as the real test — the peg holds on a buffer soft imports are masking, not inflows are rebuilding.

chart_read.signal: USD/BDT firmed to 122.78 from 123.20 as importer dollar demand ebbed; reserves $36.42bn, the export line soft against a $1.77bn trade gap.
chart_read.context: Reserves on the 31 Jul print, cover 6.28mo — 17 days old, the August refresh still awaited.
chart_read.implication: Treasury: the peg's calm is demand-led, not earnings-led — watch the reserve refresh over the daily spot as inflows thin.

title: Remittance
verdict: Remittance holds $2.82bn — a second month under $3bn.

risk: Earned dollars softening while reserves draw and the energy bill climbs
The margin over the $1.77bn trade gap no longer growing

runway.unit: monthly cover over the trade gap

banker_read.verdict: July remittance held $2.82bn — a second straight month under $3bn — while the buffer stops rebuilding: reserves $36.42bn on the 31 Jul print, cover 6.28mo. The margin over the $1.77bn trade gap has flattened near $1.05bn, both hard-currency engines soft as RMG-to-EU exports run off 16.4%.

tldr: July remittance holds $2.82bn, a second straight month under $3bn.
analysis: The earned-dollar engine is idling. July remittance held $2.82bn — a second straight month under $3bn, flat across the window — and it is not alone: RMG exports to the EU fell 16.4% in H1. Both hard-currency engines are soft at once. What masks it is the demand side: USD/BDT firmed to 122.78 as importer dollar demand ebbed — a cooling economy, private credit dead at a 33-year-low 4.98%, drawing fewer dollars than it earns. That is why the peg looks calm. But calm built on weak imports is not calm built on strong inflows. Reserves stood at $36.42bn on the 31 Jul print, cover 6.28mo, the August refresh overdue, and remittance's margin over the $1.77bn trade gap has flattened near $1.05bn. The book reads the runway as finite: long 122.78, but positioned for the reserve refresh, not the daily spot, to set direction.

metrics.sub: July print — a second month under $3bn, flat all window
metrics.label: Monthly Remittance
